Who we work with

Three very different briefs

Builders

You need the block cleared, dug and handed over on the date you were given, because the frame is already booked. One contractor across demolition, excavation and cartage means one programme to chase.

Developers

Unit blocks, walk ups, shops and service stations, where asbestos, underground tanks and contaminated soil all have to be dealt with before a basement can start.

Homeowners

Knockdown rebuilds, garages, sheds and pools. Usually the first time you have done this, so we explain what happens, in what order, and what the site will look like when we leave.

Plant and haulage

Every machine the job needs, and the trucks to clear it

Excavation and haulage are run by the one team, so the dig, the cartage and the material coming back are sequenced together rather than booked job by job.

How a job runs

From first site visit to a block you can build on

Every site differs, but the order rarely does. Knowing what comes next is usually the difference between a programme that holds and one that slips.

Site assessment

We walk the site, check access, services and what the structure is actually made of, then quote against what we find.

Approvals and notifications

The approvals, service disconnections and notifications a site needs before anyone starts. We will tell you what your job requires and who has to lodge it.

Hazardous material

Asbestos identified, then sampled, removed and cleared by licensed specialists and disposed of at a licensed facility before demolition proper.

Demolition and dig

The structure comes down, the ground comes out, and the spoil goes straight onto a truck rather than sitting on the verge.

Clean handover

Site cut to level, compacted, swept and handed back ready for set out, with the paperwork that goes with it.
